question: Can ordinary monolithic networks learn an exponentially large compositional task family from sub-exponentially many tasks, and what data coverage and internal representation accompany success?

key_findings.claim: Scaling distinct training tasks and model capacity produces held-out compositional generalization in the controlled task families.
key_findings.evidence: Across module count, components per task, held-out fraction, MLP width, and depth, held-out R-squared rises toward the paper's 0.95 success threshold. The number of training tasks required grows more slowly than the combinatorial task family, and the trend repeats for transformers, deeper teachers, and a compositional grid-policy family.

key_findings.claim: A standard ReLU MLP has a parameter-efficient compositional solution for the paper's hyperteacher class.
key_findings.evidence: The constructive approximation theorem gives uniform epsilon approximation on compact inputs using O(1/sqrt(epsilon)+M) neurons for M bounded modules, linear rather than exponential in module count; the appendix extends the construction to multilayer hyperteachers.

key_findings.claim: Information-preserving task encodings need not expose constituents linearly at the input for composition to emerge.
key_findings.evidence: With M=16 and K=3, identity, orthogonal, and language encodings reach held-out R-squared 1.00; invertible-network, interval-shuffle, and few-shot encodings reach 0.95, 0.98, and 0.97. Their third-layer constituent decoders reach R-squared 0.90-0.99 even when input decodability is only -0.23 to 0.73.

key_findings.claim: Coverage, not raw frequency symmetry, determines whether scaling can identify the modules.
key_findings.evidence: Removing compositional or connected support prevents reliable generalization. A few popular modules cause little harm, whereas making a few modules rare causes a visible drop, consistent with those constituents remaining underdetermined or memorized.

key_findings.claim: Constituent decodability is necessary in a broad functional sense and empirically correlates with successful image composition, but linearity is an empirical strengthening.
key_findings.evidence: Theorem 4.1 constructs a decoder with success at least 1-sqrt(delta) when tasks are accurately predicted and functionally distinguishable. In trained MLPs, linear decodability tightly tracks held-out performance, and across four diffusion image generators average hidden constituent decodability correlates with VLM-judged composition success.

method.core_idea: Treat composition as a controlled family of tasks generated by combinations of modules, hold out combinations, and scale the diversity of observed tasks and the capacity of a generic student rather than building composition into its architecture.
method.mechanism: Linear hypernetworks generate ReLU task functions from K-of-M module combinations. MLP or decoder-only transformer students receive data plus an identity, projected, language, invertible, shuffled, or few-shot task encoding. Experiments vary support, data, width, and depth; theory constructs an efficient MLP approximant and derives task decodability from functional distinguishability.
assumptions: The task encoder is injective and therefore fully specifies the task in the main setting.
The composition operator is injective and has sub-exponential program complexity in the number of components.
Training task support includes every module and connects module subsets sufficiently to identify their effects.
The hyperteacher's module matrices are uniformly bounded and the approximation domain is compact.
Synthetic task generators and held-out combinations capture relevant aspects of real compositional generalization.

techniques.role: Tests new combinations of individually observed modules rather than random examples from known tasks.
Varies M, K, task holdout fraction, model width, and depth to separate combinatorial family size from observed-task count.
Provides exact module ground truth while spanning a flexible family of neural task functions.
Creates compositional, disconnected, popular-module, and rare-module training supports.
Fits linear probes on hidden activations and tests them only on held-out task combinations.
Builds a generic MLP that approximates bilinear constituent-weight interactions with size linear in M.

evaluations.setting: Single-layer hyperteacher across M, K, and task holdout
evaluations.result: Performance rises with task count and required training tasks grow sub-exponentially versus total combinations
evaluations.baseline: Small training supports and smaller MLPs

evaluations.setting: M=16, K=3 hyperteacher, six task encodings

evaluations.result: Disconnected, non-compositional, and rare-module support degrade performance
Identity/language reach 0.92 accuracy; nonlinear encodings 0.82-0.84, with decoder R-squared 0.90-0.98

evaluations.setting: Four diffusion image models over synthetic concept-composition families
evaluations.metric: VLM-judged success versus linear constituent decodability
evaluations.result: Clear positive correlation across task families and models
evaluations.baseline: Harder task families show both lower decodability and lower generation success

limitations: The main evidence uses synthetic teachers with known modules, unlimited fresh samples per task, and fully specified unambiguous tasks.
The approximation theorem proves existence, not that SGD finds the linear-size generalizing solution or how much data it requires.
The paper calls the observed training-task scaling sub-exponential over a finite experimental range without estimating an asymptotic exponent or uncertainty on that law.
Three seeds and R-squared thresholds provide limited evidence about transition sharpness and hyperparameter robustness.
Linear decodability can correlate with success without being causally used by the model, and the general theorem guarantees only an arbitrary decoder.
Image-generation success is labeled by a vision-language model, creating correlated evaluator error and no controlled intervention on decoded constituents.
Real data rarely reveal the true module basis or permit designed connected support, so the prescription is hard to operationalize directly.
failure_modes: Scaling repeats already popular combinations while leaving a rare constituent underidentified.
An input encoding is technically injective but computationally difficult to invert within the available model and data budget.
A large model memorizes observed task IDs when the support fails to force a shared modular explanation.
A linear probe decodes constituents from incidental information that the prediction path does not use.
A held-out split leaks near-duplicate combinations or constituent co-occurrence statistics, overstating systematicity.
reusable_insights: Measure data scale as coverage of distinct mechanisms and combinations, not just sample count.
Audit the support hypergraph: every constituent must appear and constituent groups must be connected through shared combinations.
Compare task information at the input and at intermediate layers to detect learned linearization of nonlinear context.
Pair an existence theorem with an optimization test; representability alone does not explain emergence under SGD.
Use rare-constituent interventions to distinguish harmful undercoverage from benign popularity imbalance.
open_questions: Under what optimization and initialization conditions does SGD select the linear-size compositional solution over task memorization?
Can training-task sample complexity be bounded in M, K, support connectivity, noise, and encoding complexity?
Does constituent decodability causally mediate prediction, as tested by interventions or representation editing?
How can connected support be estimated when real-world constituents are latent and possibly hierarchical?
Do the scaling curves persist for ambiguous instructions, noisy labels, long compositions, and autoregressive sequence tasks?

competitive_landscape.title: Discovering Modular Solutions that Generalize Compositionally
competitive_landscape.relationship: Uses the same hyperteacher and support-identification framing to show modular hypernetworks generalize where tested monolithic meta-learners fail.
competitive_landscape.difference: The present paper demonstrates that sufficiently scaled generic MLPs can eventually succeed and gives a linear-size existence construction, trading modular sample efficiency for scale.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Generalization from First Principles
competitive_landscape.relationship: Derives support and architecture conditions for generalization from a compositional data-generating process.
competitive_landscape.difference: It emphasizes explicit structural conditions; this paper focuses on monolithic-network scaling and learned task-constituent linearization within controlled task families.

competitive_landscape.title: Data Factors for Better Compositional Generalization
competitive_landscape.relationship: Shows Transformer compositional generalization depends on training-set scale, diversity, complexity, difficulty, and repetition frequency in language tasks.
competitive_landscape.difference: It studies empirical NLP data factors; this paper isolates module-support topology, proves an MLP approximation bound, and probes constituent representations.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Abilities Emerge Multiplicatively: Exploring Diffusion Models on a Synthetic Task
competitive_landscape.relationship: Finds diffusion-model composition depends on data-generating structure and constituent frequency and can show sudden multiplicative emergence.
competitive_landscape.difference: It explains output emergence through constituent-task performance; this paper relates success to support coverage, model scale, and hidden constituent decodability.

competitive_landscape.title: Compositional Visual Generation with Composable Diffusion Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: Builds explicit energy-based modularity into diffusion sampling to generate unseen compositions.
competitive_landscape.difference: It changes the inference architecture to guarantee composition; the present paper asks when an ordinary monolithic network discovers composition through scale.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The paper claims generic MLPs acquire compositional generalization through data and model scale, need only linearly many neurons for a broad hyperteacher class, and internally expose task constituents when successful.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Sections 3-4 combine controlled scale/support sweeps, Theorems 3.1 and 4.1, cross-encoding probes, and image-generation correlations.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The novelty lies in reversing the same authors' earlier modular-versus-monolithic result by exposing the scale regime where monolithic models work, plus linking this to linearized task codes. Claims should remain limited to controlled task families because neither SGD selection nor real-world module discovery is theoretically resolved.

reviewer_notes: Read all 34 extracted pages except page 34, which the source index marks as missing after OCR and is not cited here; the readable appendix contains proofs, replications, and experimental details. Primary arXiv/OpenReview competitors were checked on 2026-08-23.
